traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md are implemented and verified by tests.
1) File-Level Template: ensureFileSupportsAnnotation, buildSupportsTemplateComment, and insertSupportsTemplate automatically add a file-level @supports JSDoc when missing. The inserted template matches the story’s example (`docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ`) and includes a TODO line explaining what to fill in. Tests assert the exact before/after code, proving correct insertion and placeholder quality.
2) Format Fixes: normalizeReqId and normalizeReqPrefixInDescription, wired via handleItOrTestCall, fix malformed `[REQ-XXX]` prefixes for spacing, delimiters (underscore to hyphen), case (lowercase to uppercase), and parentheses to brackets. Tests cover all specified malformed cases, each with an expected `output` string that matches the story’s requirements.
3) Safety and Preservation: Auto-fixes only change comments and test name string literals, never implementation code. Quote style and escaping are preserved via createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw, and shebang lines are preserved at the top of files. The rule only attaches fixers when a clear existing REQ ID can be normalized and when auto-fix flags are enabled, and it does not add prefixes where none exist. This satisfies REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, and REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE.
4) Integration and UX: The rule is declared fixable and uses ESLint’s fixer API, so ESLint --fix applies these changes. Options autoFixTestTemplate, autoFixTestPrefixFormat, and testSupportsTemplate are implemented with schema and defaults as specified. The template and normalized prefixes follow consistent, documented conventions, making them easy for developers to complete.
5) Tests and Documentation: Dedicated RuleTester cases in tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts are explicitly linked to this story via @supports, and the full Jest suite passes. Combined with the story markdown and inline JSDoc, this fulfills the documentation and Definition of Done items.
Based on the concrete implementation, targeted tests, and passing CI test results, this story is fully and correctly implemented.
